title: Time to event
description: How long until something happens (a cancellation, a failure), when for some rows it has not happened yet.
question: Which decisions does DCLab reach on a time to event problem (How long until something happens (a cancellation, a failure), when for some rows it has not happened yet), and do they hold?
hypothesis: Each decision a careful data scientist reaches on this kind of problem holds on every seed of the kind's replica.
setup_summary: The time to event kind's replica on seeds 0, 1, 2, brought as a person would; its own machine in dclab_core solve it, and each decision is checked on the finished run. No model is called.

claims.statement: Time to event: on 3 of 3 seeds every decision held (95% interval over seeds [0.439, 1.0]); 21 of 21 decision checks held.
limitations: Invented replicas with planted traps, three seeds: what the kind decides, not how well it does on real data.
Checks on one seed share its data, so they are not independent: the interval over seeds is the honest one.
The engine does not run this kind yet: it runs as a library (dclab_core).
